standard_prerequisites.name: The quotient by a power of a prime ideal of dimension zero inherits a normalized dualizing complex
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source lines 3426)
standard_prerequisites.use: Replaces the ring by a quotient in which the ideal has become zero, without changing the localized complex.

standard_prerequisites.name: The degree confinement for the cohomology of a normalized dualizing complex
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source lines 3428-3429)
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that only the degree equal to minus the dimension can be nonzero.

standard_prerequisites.name: The localization of a dualizing complex at a prime is dualizing over the local ring
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source lines 3430-3432)
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows the remaining cohomology module is nonzero.

core_obligations: Make the ideal zero: since the local ring at the minimal prime has dimension zero some power of the prime dies there, and the internal hom out of the quotient by that power computes a normalized dualizing complex for the quotient whose localization is the same, so one may replace the ring by that quotient (proof lines 3413-3426)
Bound the degree: in the quotient the dimension is the given integer e, and the degree confinement shows that the localized cohomology can be nonzero only in degree minus e (proof lines 3427-3429)
Nonvanishing: the localization of the complex is a dualizing complex over the nonzero local ring, so that module cannot vanish (proof lines 3430-3433)
proof_roadmap: A_p 维数为零 ⇒ 存在 n 使 p^n A_p = 0；令 B = A/p^n、ω_B^• = RHom_A(B, ω_A^•)。
由 base-change-RHom：(ω_B^•)_p = (ω_A^•)_p；再由 normalized-quotient 可把 A 换成 B，此时 dim A = e。
由 sitting-in-degrees (1)(2)：(ω_A^•)_p 只在 i = -e 可能非零；又由 dualizing-localize 它仍是对偶复形，故该模非零 ⇒ 充要。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement pins down the single degree in which the cohomology of a normalized dualizing complex localized at a minimal prime is nonzero, namely minus the dimension of the quotient by that prime (author lemma at source lines 3402-3410, label lemma-nonvanishing-generically-local). The proof (source lines 3412-3434) kills a power of the prime by replacing the ring with the corresponding quotient through an internal hom that leaves the localized complex unchanged, reads the dimension off that quotient, confines the degree by the sitting in degrees statement and gets nonvanishing from the local complex being dualizing (proof lines 3430-3433). The reduction to the quotient is the substance. H3.
